newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was lower against the dollar in late trading on Thursday following dollar short-covering by offshore players, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore players, mainly from Singapore, were seen covering their short dollar positions after speculation for a band widening failed to materialise.
He said foreign players had speculated for a band widening in the past two days which lifted the rupiah.
Spot rupiah was at 2,392.0/93.0 at 0845 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,391.0/92.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,391.25/92.00 and 2,391.0/91.6, respectively.
The U.S. bank dealer said offshore players were forced to unload the rupiah as its interest rates continued to soften in the interbank market on sustained ample supply.
"Short-term rates are traded around par. Why should people hold the rupiah at present?" the dealer asked.
Overnight rupiah fell to 3.5/4.0 percent in the afternoon.

The central bank lowered its bilateral rates for short-term papers (SBIs) by 25 basis points on Thursday and also removed offer on three-month papers. One state bank dealer said the move might indicate further attempts by the central bank to slow down short-term foreign capital inflows.
The bank offered seven-day SBIs at 6.75 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
Overnight swaps were at par/0.05 and tom/next at 0.20/0.35.
Dealers said swap rates remained soft on ample liquidity.
One-month swaps were at 10.00/10.50, two at 23.00/24.00, three at 34.5/35.5 and six at 72.50/74.50 points.

The rupiah was softer against the dollar in the morning following comments by the Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that he was concerned about the risks of inflation as well as the dramatic increase in stock prices.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,381/2,573 and the conversion band 2,381/2,429 on Thursday after raising them by one point on Tuesday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by three points the previous week.
